response: The initial duration of copyright has varied over time and across different jurisdictions. However, in the United States, the Copyright Act of 1790, which was the first federal copyright law, provided for an initial term of 14 years of copyright protection. This could be renewed for one additional 14-year term if the author was still alive. Over the years, the duration of copyright has been extended significantly. As of the Copyright Act of 1976, the general rule is that copyright protection lasts for the life of the author plus 70 years after their death. For works made for hire or anonymous works, the term is 95 years from publication or 120 years from creation, whichever is shorter.
